paragraphs.text: Now there were some present at that very season who told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
paragraphs.original: Παρῆσαν δέ τινες ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ καιρῷ ἀπαγγέλλοντες αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν Γαλιλαίων ὧν τὸ αἷμα Πιλᾶτος ἔμιξεν μετὰ τῶν θυσιῶν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Parēsan de tines en autō tō kairō apangellontes autō peri tōn Galilaiōn hōn to haima Pilatos emixen meta tōn thysiōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto them, Think ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they have suffered these things?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Δοκεῖτε ὅτι οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι οὗτοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ πάντας τοὺς Γαλιλαίους ἐγένοντο, ὅτι ταῦτα πεπόνθασιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis eipen autois· Dokeite hoti hoi Galilaioi houtoi hamartōloi para pantas tous Galilaious egenonto, hoti tauta peponthasin;

paragraphs.text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all in like manner perish.
paragraphs.original: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἐὰν μὴ μετανοῆτε πάντες ὁμοίως ἀπολεῖσθε.
paragraphs.translit: ouchi, legō hymin, allʼ ean mē metanoēte pantes homoiōs apoleisthe.

paragraphs.text: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them, think ye that they were offenders above all the men that dwell in Jerusalem?
paragraphs.original: ἢ ἐκεῖνοι οἱ δεκαοκτὼ ἐφʼ οὓς ἔπεσεν ὁ πύργος ἐν τῷ Σιλωὰμ καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτούς, δοκεῖτε ὅτι αὐτοὶ ὀφειλέται ἐγένοντο παρὰ πάντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Ἰερουσαλήμ;
paragraphs.translit: ē ekeinoi hoi dekaoktō ephʼ hous epesen ho pyrgos en tō Silōam kai apekteinen autous, dokeite hoti autoi opheiletai egenonto para pantas tous anthrōpous tous katoikountas Ierousalēm;

paragraphs.text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.
paragraphs.original: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἐὰν μὴ μετανοῆτε πάντες ὡσαύτως ἀπολεῖσθε.
paragraphs.translit: ouchi, legō hymin, allʼ ean mē metanoēte pantes hōsautōs apoleisthe.

paragraphs.text: And he spake this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came seeking fruit thereon, and found none.
paragraphs.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ ταύτην τὴν παραβολήν. Συκῆν εἶχέν τις πεφυτευμένην ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἦλθεν ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ οὐχ εὗρεν.
paragraphs.translit: Elegen de tautēn tēn parabolēn. Sykēn eichen tis pephyteumenēn en tō ampelōni autou, kai ēlthen zētōn karpon en autē kai ouch heuren.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto the vinedresser, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why doth it also cumber the ground?
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὸν ἀμπελουργόν· Ἰδοὺ τρία ἔτη ἀφʼ οὗ ἔρχομαι ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν τῇ συκῇ ταύτῃ καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκω· ἔκκοψον αὐτήν· ἱνατί καὶ τὴν γῆν καταργεῖ;
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros ton ampelourgon· Idou tria etē aphʼ hou erchomai zētōn karpon en tē sykē tautē kai ouch heuriskō· ekkopson autēn· hinati kai tēn gēn katargei;

paragraphs.text: And he answering saith unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἄφες αὐτὴν καὶ τοῦτο τὸ ἔτος, ἕως ὅτου σκάψω περὶ αὐτὴν καὶ βάλω κόπρια·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis legei autō· Kyrie, aphes autēn kai touto to etos, heōs hotou skapsō peri autēn kai balō kopria·

paragraphs.text: and if it bear fruit thenceforth, [well]; but if not, thou shalt cut it down.
paragraphs.original: κἂν μὲν ποιήσῃ καρπὸν εἰς τὸ μέλλον— εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἐκκόψεις αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: kan men poiēsē karpon eis to mellon— ei de mēge, ekkopseis autēn.

paragraphs.text: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath day.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de didaskōn en mia tōn synagōgōn en tois sabbasin.

paragraphs.text: And behold, a woman that had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years; and she was bowed together, and could in no wise lift herself up.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη δεκαοκτώ, καὶ ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou gynē pneuma echousa astheneias etē dekaoktō, kai ēn synkyptousa kai mē dynamenē anakypsai eis to panteles.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus saw her, he called her, and said to her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Γύναι, ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου,
paragraphs.translit: idōn de autēn ho Iēsous prosephōnēsen kai eipen autē· Gynai, apolelysai tēs astheneias sou,

paragraphs.text: And he laid his hands upon her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας· καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη, καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai epethēken autē tas cheiras· kai parachrēma anōrthōthē, kai edoxazen ton theon.

paragraphs.text: And the ruler of the synagogue, being moved with indignation because Jesus had healed on the sabbath, answered and said to the multitude, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the day of the sabbath.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι· ἐν αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho archisynagōgos, aganaktōn hoti tō sabbatō etherapeusen ho Iēsous, elegen tō ochlō hoti Hex hēmerai eisin en hais dei ergazesthai· en autais oun erchomenoi therapeuesthe kai mē tē hēmera tou sabbatou.

paragraphs.text: But the Lord answered him, and said, Ye hypocrites, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν· Ὑποκριταί, ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει;
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē de autō ho kyrios kai eipen· Hypokritai, hekastos hymōn tō sabbatō ou lyei ton boun autou ē ton onon apo tēs phatnēs kai apagagōn potizei;

paragraphs.text: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound, lo, [these] eighteen years, to have been loosed from this bond on the day of the sabbath?
paragraphs.original: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;
paragraphs.translit: tautēn de thygatera Abraam ousan, hēn edēsen ho Satanas idou deka kai oktō etē, ouk edei lythēnai apo tou desmou toutou tē hēmera tou sabbatou;

paragraphs.text: And as he said these things, all his adversaries were put to shame: and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντος αὐτοῦ κατῃσχύνοντο πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἔχαιρεν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai tauta legontos autou katēschynonto pantes hoi antikeimenoi autō, kai pas ho ochlos echairen epi pasin tois endoxois tois ginomenois hypʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: He said therefore, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I liken it?
paragraphs.original: Ἔλεγεν οὖν· Τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν;
paragraphs.translit: Elegen oun· Tini homoia estin hē basileia tou theou, kai tini homoiōsō autēn;

paragraphs.text: It is like unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his own garden; and it grew, and became a tree; and the birds of the heaven lodged in the branches thereof.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοία ἐστὶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔβαλεν εἰς κῆπον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ηὔξησεν καὶ ἐγένετο εἰς δένδρον, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: homoia estin kokkō sinapeōs, hon labōn anthrōpos ebalen eis kēpon heautou, kai ēuxēsen kai egeneto eis dendron, kai ta peteina tou ouranou kateskēnōsen en tois kladois autou.

paragraphs.text: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ πάλιν εἶπεν· Τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: Kai palin eipen· Tini homoiōsō tēn basileian tou theou;

paragraphs.text: It is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοία ἐστὶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἔκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
paragraphs.translit: homoia estin zymē, hēn labousa gynē ekrypsen eis aleurou sata tria heōs hou ezymōthē holon.

paragraphs.text: And he went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and journeying on unto Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ διεπορεύετο κατὰ πόλεις καὶ κώμας διδάσκων καὶ πορείαν ποιούμενος εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai dieporeueto kata poleis kai kōmas didaskōn kai poreian poioumenos eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: And one said unto him, Lord, are they few that are saved? And he said unto them,
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de tis autō· Kyrie, ei oligoi hoi sōzomenoi; ho de eipen pros autous·

paragraphs.text: Strive to enter in by the narrow door: for many, I say unto you, shall seek to enter in, and shall not be able.
paragraphs.original: Ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας, ὅτι πολλοί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν,
paragraphs.translit: Agōnizesthe eiselthein dia tēs stenēs thyras, hoti polloi, legō hymin, zētēsousin eiselthein kai ouk ischysousin,

paragraphs.text: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, open to us; and he shall answer and say to you, I know you not whence ye are;
paragraphs.original: ἀφʼ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἄρξησθε ἔξω ἑστάναι καὶ κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν· καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ.
paragraphs.translit: aphʼ hou an egerthē ho oikodespotēs kai apokleisē tēn thyran, kai arxēsthe exō hestanai kai krouein tēn thyran legontes· Kyrie, anoixon hēmin· kai apokritheis erei hymin· Ouk oida hymas pothen este.

paragraphs.text: then shall ye begin to say, We did eat and drink in thy presence, and thou didst teach in our streets;
paragraphs.original: τότε ἄρξεσθε λέγειν· Ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας·
paragraphs.translit: tote arxesthe legein· Ephagomen enōpion sou kai epiomen, kai en tais plateiais hēmōn edidaxas·

paragraphs.text: and he shall say, I tell you, I know not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐρεῖ λέγων ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα πόθεν ἐστέ· ἀπόστητε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, πάντες ἐργάται ἀδικίας.
paragraphs.translit: kai erei legōn hymin· Ouk oida pothen este· apostēte apʼ emou, pantes ergatai adikias.

paragraphs.text: There shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast forth without.
paragraphs.original: ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων, ὅταν ὄψησθε Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ καὶ πάντας τοὺς προφήτας ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑμᾶς δὲ ἐκβαλλομένους ἔξω.
paragraphs.translit: ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn, hotan opsēsthe Abraam kai Isaak kai Iakōb kai pantas tous prophētas en tē basileia tou theou, hymas de ekballomenous exō.

paragraphs.text: And they shall come from the east and west, and from the north and south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἥξουσιν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν καὶ ἀπὸ βορρᾶ καὶ νότου καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hēxousin apo anatolōn kai dysmōn kai apo borra kai notou kai anaklithēsontai en tē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And behold, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἰσὶν ἔσχατοι οἳ ἔσονται πρῶτοι, καὶ εἰσὶν πρῶτοι οἳ ἔσονται ἔσχατοι.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou eisin eschatoi hoi esontai prōtoi, kai eisin prōtoi hoi esontai eschatoi.

paragraphs.text: In that very hour there came certain Pharisees, saying to him, Get thee out, and go hence: for Herod would fain kill thee.
paragraphs.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθάν τινες Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε καὶ πορεύου ἐντεῦθεν, ὅτι Ἡρῴδης θέλει σε ἀποκτεῖναι.
paragraphs.translit: En autē tē hōra prosēlthan tines Pharisaioi legontes autō· Exelthe kai poreuou enteuthen, hoti Hērōdēs thelei se apokteinai.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Go and say to that fox, Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures to-day and to-morrow, and the third [day] I am perfected.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες εἴπατε τῇ ἀλώπεκι ταύτῃ· Ἰδοὺ ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια καὶ ἰάσεις ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ τελειοῦμαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois· Poreuthentes eipate tē alōpeki tautē· Idou ekballō daimonia kai iaseis apotelō sēmeron kai aurion, kai tē tritē teleioumai.

paragraphs.text: Nevertheless I must go on my way to-day and to-morrow and the [day] following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν δεῖ με σήμερον καὶ αὔριον καὶ τῇ ἐχομένῃ πορεύεσθαι, ὅτι οὐκ ἐνδέχεται προφήτην ἀπολέσθαι ἔξω Ἰερουσαλήμ.
paragraphs.translit: plēn dei me sēmeron kai aurion kai tē echomenē poreuesthai, hoti ouk endechetai prophētēn apolesthai exō Ierousalēm.

paragraphs.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets, and stoneth them that are sent unto her! how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen [gathereth] her own brood under her wings, and ye would not!
paragraphs.original: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν— ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυνάξαι τὰ τέκνα σου ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις τὴν ἑαυτῆς νοσσιὰν ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε.
paragraphs.translit: Ierousalēm Ierousalēm, hē apokteinousa tous prophētas kai lithobolousa tous apestalmenous pros autēn— posakis ēthelēsa episynaxai ta tekna sou hon tropon ornis tēn heautēs nossian hypo tas pterygas, kai ouk ēthelēsate.

paragraphs.text: Behold, your house is left unto you [desolate]: and I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν. λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἴδητέ με ἕως ἥξει ὅτε εἴπητε· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: idou aphietai hymin ho oikos hymōn. legō de hymin, ou mē idēte me heōs hēxei hote eipēte· Eulogēmenos ho erchomenos en onomati kyriou.
